source.title: Deep Networks Always Grok and Here is Why
source.authors: Ahmed Imtiaz Humayun; Randall Balestriero; R. Baraniuk

record.tranche_reason: Reports training-accuracy trajectories for CNNs on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 and a ResNet18 on CIFAR-10, bearing on whether training reaches interpolation; it does not directly compare training recipes for training error.
record.gate_note: Training-accuracy curves are shown in Figures 1 and 6. Other reported outcomes concern test/adversarial accuracy or local complexity, not the claim's training-error measure.
record.test_reason: The study reports training classification accuracy for convolutional networks trained with Adam on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, matching V1's method and outcome. Section 3.1 explicitly identifies training interpolation in Figures 1 and 6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors report widespread delayed generalization or robustness and attribute these to late migration of linear-region boundaries toward decision boundaries. They acknowledge that a theoretical explanation of the local-complexity dynamics and the migration's late timing remains lacking.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Adam and standard initialization without batch normalization in its CIFAR experiments; the claim version also covers SGD, label corruption, and other model-size and stopping conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch normalization changes the reported delayed-robustness behavior; the paper says adversarial grokking does not occur or is significantly delayed with batch normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding batch normalization removes or significantly delays adversarial grokking and changes local-complexity dynamics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization can suppress delayed adversarial robustness in the tested networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing width or depth hastens region migration in MNIST MLPs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Network parameterization affects the timing of local-complexity dynamics and delayed robustness.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: Training accuracy is presented in figures without numerical values or explicit per-model training-error summaries. The 99% confidence intervals described apply to local-complexity plots, not training accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant training-error rows reported beyond R1–R3. Adversarial/test accuracy and local-complexity results do not measure V1's training-error outcome.

untested.parts: Corrupted or random CIFAR labels; systematic model-size, early-stopping and regularization comparisons; SGD. The random-label experiments use MNIST MLPs.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with convolutional depth and matched comparisons with identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, sharpness dynamics and divergence.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance; matched Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Its batch-normalization, initialization-scaling and parameterization findings concern grokking or local complexity and do not establish V2–V6. Exact training-accuracy endpoints are unavailable in the supplied figure text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test smaller models, early stopping, regularized recipes, or corrupted/random labels on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100.
